confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Marked radiographic consolidation and pulmonary opacity consistent with pneumonia pattern.
recommended_followup: Correlate with clinical presentation (fever, purulent sputum, auscultatory crackles)
Evaluate inflammatory markers (Complete Blood Count, CRP, procalcitonin)
Consider microbiological sputum cultures and blood cultures prior to targeted antimicrobial therapy
Follow-up posteroanterior (PA) chest radiograph in 4-6 weeks to assess resolution

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Focal infiltrative haziness or bronchovascular perihilar thickening suggestive of developing pneumonia.
recommended_followup: Clinical evaluation including pulse oximetry and auscultation
Serial imaging in 24-48 hours if symptoms persist or deteriorate
Consider high-resolution CT thorax if diagnostic uncertainty remains

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Equivocal opacification with borderline feature activation.
recommended_followup: Review previous radiographic studies for comparison
Repeat inspiratory chest radiograph if technique was sub-optimal
Assess clinical stability and symptom timeline

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Clear bilateral lung parenchyma without focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax.
differential_considerations: Early presentation before radiographic manifestation (clinical discordance possible)
recommended_followup: If severe respiratory symptoms are present clinically, consider chest CT as early interstitial pathology may not be visible on plain radiograph
Routine clinical monitoring

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: No definite focal consolidation detected, subtle non-specific vascular markings noted.
differential_considerations: Normal anatomical variation / mild broncho-vascular prominence
recommended_followup: Clinical correlation with respiratory symptoms and history

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Cortical disruption and radiolucent fracture line identified with high activation.
recommended_followup: Orthopedic consultation and immobilization (splint/cast)
Multi-view orthogonal radiographs (AP, lateral, oblique) to assess joint involvement
Neurovascular status assessment distal to injury site

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Potential cortical irregularity or periosteal reaction observed.
differential_considerations: Nutrient foramen or anatomical overlap artifact
recommended_followup: Obtain dedicated orthogonal views
Re-evaluate in 7-10 days with repeat radiograph if focal point tenderness persists

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Intact cortical margins and alignment throughout visible osseous structures.
differential_considerations: Occult fracture not readily apparent on initial projection
recommended_followup: Symptomatic management (RICE protocol: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation)
Follow-up evaluation if unable to bear weight or if pain worsens

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Focal hyperintense intracranial lesion or parenchymal mass effect detected on structural neuroimaging.
differential_considerations: Secondary metastatic lesion / Cerebritis with perilesional vasogenic edema
recommended_followup: Urgent Neurosurgical and Neuro-Oncology consultation
Contrast-enhanced T1/T2/FLAIR MRI with MR Spectrometry / Perfusion weighting
Correlate with neurologic exam, cranial nerve testing, and ICP evaluation

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Suspicious signal intensity alteration or localized ventricular asymmetry requiring expert radiologic review.
differential_considerations: Subacute ischemic change or demyelinating plaque
recommended_followup: Thin-slice 3T MRI with IV gadolinium contrast
Formal neuroradiologist subspecialty overread

confidence_bands.clinical_summary: Symmetric cerebral hemispheres, intact sulcal-gyral pattern, and unremarkable ventricular caliber.
recommended_followup: Correlate with clinical symptoms; outpatient neurology follow-up if headaches persist
No acute surgical intervention indicated
